summary: Create a Public connection (integration) in Notion's developer portal to get OAuth credentials. The docs describe no review step for using it; Marketplace listing is separate.

difficulty.label: Self-serve
difficulty.rationale: Creating a public connection with a redirect URI is self-serve in what we read. But an image caption on Notion's authorization page says the Authorization URL field only 'populates after a public connection is submitted for review', so a review step may sit between creating and using it. Marketplace listing is reviewed separately.

effort.basis: Our estimate. No source states a setup time (Composio's guide shows only a 4-minute reading time).

wait.display: 5-10 business days to hear back (Marketplace listing only)
wait.statement: Only applies if you list on the Notion Marketplace. 5-10 business days is Notion's stated time to hear back; our calendar-day range (7-14) is a conversion.
wait.headline: 5-10 business days
wait.note: Only for a Marketplace listing. Whether a plain public connection needs review is still an open question.

composio_managed.note: Composio's Notion toolkit page lists OAuth2 and API key and says 'Composio-managed OAuth available.' So a developer can connect users without registering their own provider app first; register your own only for your own branding, scopes or rate limits.

requirements.text: A Notion workspace to act as the development workspace (Composio's guide says a free workspace is sufficient).
Required fields: connection name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope, capabilities.
Only public connections with installation scope 'Any workspace' can be listed on the Marketplace. The scope cannot be changed after creation, so choose it deliberately.

scopes_and_access.text: Installation scope is either 'Any workspace' or 'Selected workspaces only' and cannot be changed after creation. Marketplace eligibility depends on choosing Any workspace.
Access is limited to pages explicitly shared with the integration.

gotchas.text: Pick the installation scope carefully: it cannot be changed after creation.
Redirect URIs must be HTTPS and exact match: no trailing slash, wildcards or fragments.
API-key (internal integration) auth only works with Internal integrations; Public integrations must use OAuth.

steps.title: Open the developer portal
steps.detail: Go to the Notion developer portal, Build > Public connections.

steps.title: Create the connection
steps.detail: Create new connection; set name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope and capabilities (only what you need).
steps.why_not_agent: Needs your signed-in Notion session; scope choice is permanent.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret
steps.detail: Open the Configuration tab to get the OAuth client ID and secret. Treat the secret like a password.
steps.why_not_agent: Secret must go straight to your secret store.

steps.title: Create the auth config in Composio
steps.detail: Create auth config > Notion > OAuth2 > 'Use your own developer authentication' > enter client ID, secret and the same redirect URI.

blockers.symptom: Connected but the agent cannot see your pages
blockers.likely_cause: Notion integrations only see pages explicitly shared with them.
blockers.fix: Share the relevant pages or databases with the integration during authorization or in Notion.
blockers.escalate_when: Sharing is blocked by workspace admin settings.

review_process.text: Notion reviews every Marketplace listing submission; it sends feedback and you can resubmit.
Notion says to expect to hear back within 5-10 business days by email. That is a response time, not a guaranteed approval time.

next_actions: Decide Any workspace vs Selected workspaces before submitting.

agent_can: Explain field choices and create the Composio auth config once given credentials securely.
you_must: Sign in and create the connection.

uncertainties: OPEN QUESTION to settle in the first hands-on test: Notion's authorization page has a caption saying the Authorization URL populates after a public connection is submitted for review. We could not tell whether that is a light submission or the full Marketplace review.
Notion's portal UI has changed recently (docs point to app.notion.com/developers/connections); third-party screenshots may be stale.
The authorization page does not name a privacy-policy requirement; the listing page lists name, description, category, tags, images and logo.
